questions.q: What are the major causes of the depletion of forest and wildlife resources in India?
answer: India's rich biodiversity has come under great pressure, mainly from human activity.

answer.text: Large areas of forest were cleared for cultivation, especially during colonial rule when railways, plantations and commercial farming spread rapidly, destroying wildlife habitats.
Large dams, roads and mining have submerged and fragmented forests. Such activity destroys habitats and disturbs animal life.
Grazing, fuelwood collection, poaching and the hunting of animals for skin, horns and sport reduced many species drastically, while pollution and forest fires added to the damage.

answer: Thus habitat loss, over-exploitation and pollution together threaten India's forests and wildlife.

questions.q: How have communities helped in the conservation of forests and wildlife in India?
answer: Conservation in India has depended not only on the government but strongly on local communities.

answer.text: The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan has for generations protected blackbuck, nilgai and trees as part of its beliefs, even at the cost of their lives.
The Chipko movement in the Himalayas resisted deforestation and showed that community afforestation with local species can succeed.
Many tribal communities protect sacred groves as forests of gods and goddesses, and under Joint Forest Management villagers help restore degraded forests in return for a share of the produce.

answer: These efforts show that conservation is most effective when local people are involved.

questions.q: How does the loss of biodiversity affect human societies, especially forest-dependent communities?

answer.text: sustains ecosystems and the services people draw from them, so its loss has serious human costs.

list: Forests provide food, fuel, medicine, timber and clean water; their loss removes these directly
The decline of species disturbs food chains and the natural balance, harming farming and fisheries

answer.text: They depend on the forest for their lives.

list: Tribal and forest-dwelling people lose their livelihoods and their traditional way of life when forests vanish
Women, who gather fuel, fodder and water, have to travel far and work harder as resources shrink

questions.q: How do government programmes and legislation try to conserve forests and wildlife in India?

answer.text: protects its forests and wildlife through law and dedicated programmes.

list: The Wildlife Protection Act provides for protected species and habitats and bans hunting and trade in endangered animals
Reserved and protected forests, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves shield habitats
Project Tiger and similar efforts protect flagship animals and their ecosystems
Programmes involving local communities, and Joint Forest Management, give people a stake in protecting nearby forests
